flags: minor: thematic overlap with R032-08 and R032-09 (all three turn on 'noticed, not explained' / attending instead of copying); answering one primes the others
R032-01.notes: Final paragraph: some things 'could not be explained, only noticed.' A contradicts Lena's silence; D contradicts 'watching was the same as knowing'; B is a trap for readers who take Lena's silence as disapproval, but 'There' and the key show the opposite.

flags: minor: wrong choices A, C, D are weak; once readers see 'I did not yet know that she meant this as a kindness,' only B is positive toward the narrator
R032-02.notes: The 'kindness' line plus the arc of learning by doing support firsthand experience. Nothing supports teasing the mother or appreciating the mother's work.

flags: minor: A, B, C have no support in the text and are easy to eliminate
R032-03.notes: 'Practice for the next hundred' heard 'more like a warning' after the failure: mastery takes much longer than expected. Borderline easy/medium; rated easy because the distractors are so weak.

R032-04.notes: Moving from tacky to smooth to pushing back describes a well-kneaded, elastic dough that springs back (accurate baking science: gluten development). B is the trap, echoing 'fought me' and the everyday meaning of 'push back' (resist).

R032-05.notes: Fits Lena's pattern of quiet acts in place of words ('What she had given me instead was the key'). D gets the order wrong because the key came before the success. C tempts readers because the narrator does arrive first, but nothing shows that was Lena's purpose. A is unsupported.

flags: minor: B is contradicted outright ('furious, though not at her'), C is absurd, and only A (the literal reading of the towel) draws anyone
R032-06.notes: 'Hoped nobody would ask about' shows embarrassment at the failed first attempt.

R032-07.notes: 'Unmarked among hers' plus 'without looking twice' means the loaves were indistinguishable. D is the opposite of the passage; C overstates; B is unsupported.

flags: minor: overlaps with R032-01 (both rest on 'could not be explained, only noticed')
R032-08.notes: Paragraph 2 calls it 'the kind of thing adults say when they do not want to explain,' which is an evasion. Paragraph 7 says it could not be explained, only noticed, which makes it an accurate description. Two-paragraph synthesis; each wrong pair has its own error.

R032-09.notes: Paragraph 3 copies Lena and works faster; paragraph 5 slows down and attends to the dough. A is the opposite. C misstates the father (he gives no advice to work fast). D never happens.

R032-10.notes: The passage covers the cause (materials, loss of vegetation), then responses (roofs, trees) with tradeoffs. A is too strong, C is too narrow (no single city), and D is not discussed. Science check: the heat island is strongest on calm, clear nights; evapotranspiration cooling and the winter penalty of reflective roofs are both stated accurately.

R032-11.notes: Coatings are fast and trees are slow but offer more, so doing both pairs complementary strengths. B is the trap, contradicted by 'researchers continue to argue' and by planners favoring different options. A and D are unsupported.
